title: The Unquiet Autopsy
premise: Ansel Brightwater, an insurance investigator with a photographic memory, is hired by a nervous stranger, Corwin Vale, who pays triple rate to prove that a murder has not yet happened: the death of his uncle, shipping magnate Elias Vale, whose will Ansel is shown in advance. When Elias is found dead exactly as foretold, Ansel realizes she was hired not to prevent the murder but to witness its setup, making her the only person who can prove premeditation. As the trial of Corwin's sister approaches, Ansel decodes a shipping ledger hidden in the uncle's portrait engravings that reveals the true killer forged both the will and the prophecy. In the courtroom climax, Ansel reconstructs the murder from memory, and the killer's own ledger entries become the confession that convicts her.
about_author: Beatrix Underhill is the pen name of a former maritime insurance clerk from Hull who spent a decade auditing cargo claims before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries in which paper trails prove more damning than fingerprints.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Ansel Brightwater, in her POV, takes an unusual case: Corwin Vale pays triple to have her verify that a murder has not happened yet, producing a will dated for a death three weeks hence. Ansel, unable to resist an anomaly, accepts. The beat is wary curiosity sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: A Will Before a Death
chapters.summary: Ansel examines the pre-dated will in Elias Vale's townhouse, memorizing every clause. She notices the document references a storm that has not occurred. POV Ansel. The emotional beat is the first cold prickle of dread beneath professional detachment.

chapters.title: The Portrait Ledger
chapters.summary: In Elias's study, Ansel photographs a family portrait whose engraved frame carries odd numerical notations. She suspects a cipher but files it away. POV Ansel, with a brief interlude from housekeeper Mrs. Tarn. The beat is the reader seeing the key before the sleuth does.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Ansel interviews the Vale household staff and learns Corwin's sister, Imogen, is estranged and stands to lose everything under the new will. POV Ansel. The beat is sympathy for Imogen complicating Ansel's loyalty to her client.

chapters.title: The Date Arrives
chapters.summary: The prophesied night: Ansel stakes out the Vale house through a rising gale. Elias is found dead in his locked study, exactly as the will implied. POV Ansel, intercut with Imogen arriving uninvited. The beat is horror — the impossible made real.

chapters.title: Locked Study, Open Questions
chapters.summary: Ansel surveys the death scene before police arrive, memorizing the room: a spilled inkwell, a displaced rug fringe, a second teacup. Her photographic mind records everything. POV Ansel. The beat is controlled panic as she realizes she is now a witness to premeditation.

chapters.title: Imogen in the Dock
chapters.summary: Police arrest Imogen Vale on a tide of circumstantial evidence: fingerprints, a quarrel overheard, motive in the old will. Ansel, certain of the timeline, cannot explain how she knows. POV Ansel. The beat is guilt — her silence protects her client and condemns an innocent woman.

chapters.title: Client and Suspect
chapters.summary: Ansel confronts Corwin, who deflects with charm and produces an alibi too polished to trust. She notices his cufflink matches a button found near the study. POV Ansel. The beat is the first crack of doubt about the man who hired her.

chapters.title: The Trial Calendar
chapters.summary: The court sets Imogen's trial for six weeks out, giving Ansel a deadline. She hires a disgraced solicitor, Petra Okafor, as legal guide. POV Ansel with a Petra interlude. The beat is resolve: decode the ledger before the gavel falls.

chapters.title: Numbers in the Gilt
chapters.summary: Ansel returns to the portrait and begins systematic decryption: the engravings map to shipping routes and dates. The first decoded entry references a payment to someone named only 'T.' POV Ansel. The beat is the thrill of the hunt.

chapters.title: The Shipping Files
chapters.summary: Ansel traces Vale & Sons' ledgers to a warehouse and finds cargo manifests that don't match the portrait cipher — someone has been laundering money through phantom shipments. POV Ansel. The beat is the case widening from murder into empire.

chapters.title: A Threat in the Fog
chapters.summary: Ansel is followed home and her office is ransacked; only the portrait photograph is missing. She realizes the killer knows what she knows. POV Ansel. The beat is fear converting her from observer to target.

chapters.title: Mrs. Tarn's Confession
chapters.summary: The housekeeper admits she let someone into the study that night — a woman she assumed was Imogen, wearing Imogen's distinctive scarf. POV Mrs. Tarn, then Ansel. The beat is the frame-up becoming visible, and Ansel's fury kindling.

chapters.title: The Second Teacup
chapters.summary: Ansel reconstructs the study from memory for Petra: two cups means Elias entertained a guest he trusted. She matches the cup's porcelain to a set sold only at a charity auction — attendee list in hand. POV Ansel. The beat is the net tightening.

chapters.title: Corwin's Ledger
chapters.summary: Decoding deepens: 'T' is 'Threnody,' Corwin's private secretary, and the cipher entries record payments timed to the murder date. Ansel realizes the 'prophecy' was a plan Corwin wrote down and disguised. POV Ansel. The beat is betrayal landing like a physical blow.

chapters.title: The Client Vanishes
chapters.summary: Corwin and Threnody attempt to leave the country; Ansel intercepts Corwin at the docks and he confesses obliquely, believing she can prove nothing. POV Ansel. The beat is cold confrontation — the hunter learning she was always the quarry's backup plan.

chapters.title: Admissible Ghosts
chapters.summary: Petra warns that a decoded portrait and a photographic memory are inadmissible; they need physical corroboration. Ansel identifies the forged will's ink batch, traceable to a stationer's order signed by Threnody. POV Petra. The beat is hope built on procedure.

chapters.title: The Trial Opens
chapters.summary: Imogen's trial begins; the prosecution's case is seamless until Ansel, testifying as a witness to the will, plants the timeline discrepancy. POV Ansel in the courtroom. The beat is the first public fracture in the prosecution's story.

chapters.title: Cross-Examination
chapters.summary: Threnody, called to testify, is dismantled by Petra using the stationer's records and the scarf's provenance. Threnody breaks and implicates Corwin. POV Ansel watching. The beat is cathartic momentum.

chapters.title: The Portrait in Evidence
chapters.summary: Ansel presents the portrait cipher to the court, reading aloud the ledger entries that pre-date the murder and record its payment. The judge admits it over objection. POV Ansel. The beat is the climax's hinge: memory made into evidence.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Corwin, confronted with the ledger and his own confession at the docks recorded by a dockhand, is convicted; Imogen is acquitted and inherits, restoring the original will's spirit. Ansel closes the file. POV Ansel. The beat is justice achieved outside the law's original plan.

chapters.title: Ansel's Own Ledger
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Ansel audits herself: she took payment to prevent a murder and failed, yet ended one. She burns Corwin's retainer check and keeps only the portrait photograph. POV Ansel. The beat is quiet reckoning — identity rebuilt around memory's burden.
